oracle_provenance: Johnson-Nyquist thermal noise formula (standard textbook physics) using the exact SI-defined Boltzmann constant; independently hand-verified before implementation against the commonly cited ~1.8 uV RMS figure for a 10 kOhm resistor over the audio band. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded thermal noise floor as a physical lower bound for a claimed measured noise figure; not a full EMI/ground-loop root-cause diagnosis.

cases.question: Does a claimed noise floor matching the Johnson-Nyquist prediction at 10 kOhm/20 kHz/25C pass as physically consistent?
When a claimed noise floor is far above the thermal minimum, is that flagged as likely non-thermal (EMI/ground) rather than silently accepted?
Must a non-positive resistance be rejected rather than silently used?

When a claimed noise floor sits below the theoretical Johnson-Nyquist minimum for the declared resistance/temperature/bandwidth, is that flagged as a physical impossibility (wrong reference) rather than an unusually quiet circuit?
